captions.detailed: A 3D-printable cylindrical gear with a central hollow bore. The gear features 17 evenly spaced, tapered teeth radiating outward from the main body. The teeth are blocky at their base and taper down in width and height toward their tips, giving them a faceted, chamfered appearance.
captions.instruction: Design a customizable, parametric spur gear in OpenSCAD with adjustable parameters for the central shaft hole, outer ring diameter, and tooth profile. The user should be able to configure the number of teeth, tooth length, base width, tip width, and the tapering heights of the cogs.
captions.factory: The design is constructed using a module named 'cog'. It first creates a central ring by performing a boolean difference between two concentric cylinders (internal_diameter and hole_diameter). A for-loop then instantiates the cogs, rotating them around the Z-axis; each cog is formed using a hull operation between a base cube (no_angle, cog_base_width, cog_base_height) and a translated tip cube (.1, cog_tip_width, tip_height) to create the tapered profile.
